title: Derivatives of exponential functions
goal: Differentiate exponential functions: $e^x$ is the unique function whose slope equals its own height, and any other base $a^x$ just picks up an extra factor of $\ln a$.

beforeThis.skill: Quick check: $(e^x)' = e^x$ and $(a^x)' = a^x \ln a$. If $a > 1$ the curve grows ever steeper; if $0 < a < 1$ it decays toward $0$.

seeIt.title: What's so special about Euler's number e? (Ch. 5 of Essence of Calculus)
seeIt.creator: 3Blue1Brown
seeIt.watchFor: Shows why $e^x$ equals its own derivative and why $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x} a^x = (\ln a)a^x$.

questions.asking: Pair each labeled curve $A, B, C, D$ in the plot with its matching exponential formula from (a)–(e).
questions.statement:
Match the curves in the graph to the following functions:

  1. $y = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^x$
  2. $y = 1^x$
  3. $y = 2^x$
  4. $y = 2^{-x}$
  5. $y = 3^x$

figures.alt: Coordinate axes showing four curves passing through (0, 1): green curve A decreases from left to right toward the positive x-axis; black line D is horizontal at y = 1; blue curve B and red curve C both increase from left to right, with blue curve B rising more steeply than red curve C for x > 0.

questions.asking: Use the fact that $f(x) = a^x$ is increasing and lies above its derivative $f'(x)$ to select all true inequalities for the base $a$.
questions.statement:
The graph below shows an exponential function $f(x) = a^x$ and its derivative $f'(x)$. Choose all the options that describe the constant $a$.

  1. $a < 0$
  2. $a > 0$
  3. $a < 1$
  4. $a > 1$
  5. $a < e$
  6. $a > e$

figures.alt: Coordinate axes showing two positive increasing exponential curves: the blue upper curve is labeled y = f(x) and passes through (0, 1), while the red lower curve is labeled y = f'(x) and lies strictly below y = f(x) for all x.

questions.asking: Don't fall for the power-rule trap! The power rule $x^n \to nx^{n-1}$ only works when the exponent is a constant number, not when $x$ is in the exponent.
Write the formula obtained after differentiating $f(x) = e^x$ with respect to $x$ $180$ times in a row.
questions.statement: What is the 180th derivative of the function $f(x) = e^x$?

questions.asking: Take $\ln$ (or simplify using exponent/log rules) to see which equations turn into a straight line $y = mx + b$.
questions.statement:
Which of the following functions describe a straight line?

  1. $y = e^{3 \log x} + 1$
  2. $2y + 5 = e^{3 + \log x}$
  3. $y = e^{2x} + 4$
  4. $y = e^{\log x} 3^e + \log 2$
